questions.q: Neha committed on her branch but didn't push. Can Rohan see the commit?
options: Yes, Git shares commits automatically
No: the commit is only on her laptop until she runs git push
Only if Rohan runs git status
Only on Fridays
questions.explain: Commits are local. git push uploads them to GitHub; only then can others fetch them.

options: The first commit of the repository
The default name of the remote you cloned from, usually the repository on GitHub
A branch that can't be deleted
Your laptop's main branch
questions.explain: git clone sets up a remote called origin. origin/main is your laptop's memory of GitHub's main.

options: A Git command that downloads commits
A request on GitHub to merge a branch into main, where teammates see the diff, comment and approve
A way to delete a branch
An error message
questions.explain: It's a GitHub feature, not a Git command. You're asking the project to pull your branch in, after review.

questions.q: Right after the PR is merged on GitHub, Neha's laptop says 'Your branch is up to date with origin/main'. Why?
options: The merge failed
Her laptop only knows what it last saw of GitHub; she must git fetch (or git pull) to see the news
GitHub deleted her branch
She is on the wrong computer
questions.explain: Laptops never update by themselves. After git fetch, status says 'behind origin/main by 2 commits'.

questions.q: git fetch vs git pull: what's the difference?
options: They are the same
fetch downloads news without changing your branch; pull = fetch + merge (or rebase) into your branch
fetch uploads, pull downloads
pull only works on main
questions.explain: fetch is always safe: it only updates origin/... branches. pull also changes your current branch.

questions.q: git push says: ! [rejected] main -> main (fetch first). What should you do?
options: git push --force
Delete the repository and clone again
git pull --rebase, then git push
Wait an hour and try again
questions.explain: Someone pushed commits you don't have. Bring them in (rebase keeps a straight line), then push. --force would delete their work.

questions.q: (Going deeper) GitHub's 'Squash and merge' button does what?
options: Deletes the pull request
Turns all the branch's commits into one commit on main
Rebases main onto the branch
Merges without review
questions.explain: Squash and merge = one clean commit per pull request. 'Create a merge commit' keeps them plus a merge commit; 'Rebase and merge' replays them.

questions.q: (Going deeper) What does branch protection on main do?
options: Makes main read-only for everyone forever
Forbids direct pushes to main, so changes must come through reviewed pull requests (and passing checks)
Encrypts the branch
Backs up main every night
questions.explain: It turns the GitHub flow into a rule: no change reaches main without a pull request and the required approvals.
